items.title: docs: update README benchmarks to current temporal-reasoning results
items.body:
## Linked Issue

N/A — follow-up to #6056, which refreshed the [Memory Evaluation](https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-evaluation) page but left the README carrying the pre-temporal-reasoning numbers.

## Description

The README benchmark table and Research Highlights were out of sync with `docs/core-concepts/memory-evaluation.mdx`. This aligns them.

| Benchmark | README (before) | Docs / this PR |
|---|---|---|
| LoCoMo | 91.6 | **92.5** |
| LongMemEval | 94.8 | **94.4** |
| BEAM (1M) | 64.1 | 64.1 (unchanged) |
| BEAM (10M) | 48.6 | 48.6 (unchanged) |

Note that the README's LongMemEval score of **94.8 was not sourced by any page in `docs/`** — the current value is 94.4 (memory-evaluation) and the v3-launch value was 93.4 (migration guide / changelog). Neither is 94.8.

Also updated:

- **Research Highlights**: `+53.6 on assistant memory recall` was the old-vs-new delta against a since-superseded 100.0 score. Replaced with the current absolute, **98.2**, so it can't drift again. LoCoMo delta corrected `+20` → `+21` (71.4 → 92.5).
- **Caption**: now states the **top_200 retrieval budget** and carries the managed-platform caveat from the docs page — the scores reflect proprietary platform optimizations not in the OSS SDK, which is worth saying plainly on the OSS README.

Token counts (7.0K / 6.8K / 6.7K / 6.9K) already matched the docs (6,956 / 6,787 / 6,719 / 6,914) and are unchanged.

### One thing to confirm

The `Latency p50` column (0.88s / 1.09s / 1.00s / 1.05s) has **no source anywhere in `docs/`**, and #6056 did not touch latency. I left the values as-is rather than guess. If they were measured against the old algorithm they are now stale, and this column should either be refreshed or dropped — flagging for whoever owns the benchmark runs.

items.title: docs: rewrite README for concision, add datasets table and credits
items.body:
## What?

Rewrites `README.md` and tightens `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`benchmarks/README.md`: fewer em dashes, less AI-generated phrasing, less duplicated info, and a couple of new sections.

## Why?

- The roadmap had drifted out of sync with `main` (`num_transfer`/`num_ascend`/`num_migrate` shipped in #46 but the README still listed it as unsupported).
- The prose leaned on evaluative appositives ("the piece X needed", "the enabling piece for Y") and heavy em-dash use throughout.
- Several sections explained internal plumbing (PEP 561, zero-copy NumPy, `preprocess_*` argument threading) that a newcomer skimming the repo doesn't need on first read.
- No credit was given to TrackEval/py-motmetrics, whose algorithms and evaluation protocols this project reimplements.
- `benchmarks/README.md` quoted a stale, unsourced speedup range that didn't match the chart's actual source data.

## How?

**`README.md`**
- Shorter tagline: "Fast MOT and HOTA metrics for Python, powered by Rust."
- Highlights trimmed from 5 bullets to 3 (dropped implementation-detail bullets).
- New **Datasets** section: a compact table of all 6 adapters (format, similarity, load function) instead of prose.
- Roadmap condensed to one line per item instead of multi-line justification paragraphs, and updated to reflect #46/#47.
- New **Acknowledgments** section crediting TrackEval and py-motmetrics as the reference implementations motrics ports to Rust.
- Benchmarks section: dropped the table (redundant with the chart at the top), kept the reproducibility caveat and links.

**`CONTRIBUTING.md` / `benchmarks/README.md`**
- Dropped em dashes, tightened a few sentences.
- Reconciled `benchmarks/README.md`'s speedup range (was 3–9×/13–30×, unsourced) with `plot_speedup.py`'s `DATA` constant, which is what the chart and top-level README actually derive from.

Also fixed a stale docstring in `compat/motmetrics/metrics.py` left over from #46 that still said the switch subtypes were unsupported.

## Testing

Docs-only change (plus one docstring). `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` pass.

items.title: Set up the benchmark suite
items.body:
## Summary

Replaces the stale ITensorPkgSkeleton benchmark stub with a `BenchmarkTools` suite covering the core contraction entry points (`contract`, `contract!`) across a range of dimensions, so a regression shows up in both the small-tensor regime (dominated by the per-call label bookkeeping) and the large one (dominated by the BLAS call). The suite exposes the `SUITE` global that `AirspeedVelocity.jl`'s `benchpkg` expects, and `benchmark/README.md` documents running it directly and comparing revisions.

The suite is also run once as a smoke test in the package tests, so it cannot silently fall out of sync with the API the way the stub had (it still called the long-removed `default_contract_alg`).

items.title: Add curation benchmark: AI agents vs. manual curation
items.body:
Benchmarks Pipeline 1's two-step screening (IdentifyOriginalDataStep + IdentifyRelevanceStep) against manual curation across 16 disease scopes (9 single-cell, 7 spatial).

Headline: 90.5% recall vs. manual curation (182/201, 95% CI 85.7-93.9%), 2.12x expansion, and 244 additional candidate papers surfaced.

analysis/curation_figures.py parses data/20260413-results-analysis/*.txt and generates, in one pass:
  - Fig 1: area-proportional Euler diagram of set agreement
  - Fig 2: per-scope composition, faceted single-cell / spatial
  - Fig 3: per-scope recall with 95% Wilson confidence intervals
  - Table 1: per-scope detail (CSV + Markdown)
  - stats.json, a data-quality report, docs/curation_benchmark.md, and the README validation section

Prose numbers are interpolated from the parsed data rather than typed, and the README block is spliced between marker comments, so the text cannot drift out of sync with the figures. Regeneration is idempotent.

Precision and F1 are deliberately absent throughout: the 244 AI-only papers are unvalidated, so recall against the manual reference set is the only estimable quantity. Treating that set as false positives would invert the purpose of the pipeline.

Source files carry 8 duplicate-PMID defects, resolved by the precedence overlap > manual_only > ai_only > ssread and logged in full. Two of these (spinocerebellar ataxia, listed in both Overlap and Only-in-manual) affect the headline numbers and are worth fixing upstream.

items.title: Decision-audit platform + Evidence Loop + HingeScore calibration + provider timeouts
items.body:
11 commits — four initiatives:

### Evidence Loop — claims aligned to measured reality
- **Real benchmark numbers captured**: routingEvalBlindV3 80%, semantic 73%, blind 67%, ML 66.7%, basic 60%; routingEvalBlindV2 flagged NOT VALID in CI (no ONNX, hash-noise)
- **Retired untraceable claims**: 92% zero-shot accuracy and ~90% router accuracy removed
- **docs/CLAIM_LEDGER.md** created — every claim maps to the command that produces it
- README savings claim corrected: ~68% → ~98% (ceiling-based lab benchmark)

### Evidence Loop — post-response outcomes (new)
- **routingLog.ts**: added `provider`/`rescue`/`truncated`/`actualCost`/`actualTokens` to entries + `updateLatestLogEntry()` to patch newest entry with post-API outcomes
- **Analytics.jsx**: new "Evidence — post-response outcomes" section — rescue rate, truncation rate, actual-vs-estimate spend, real savings vs premium baseline, HingeScore band distribution. CSV export extended.
- Answers "what actually happened after routing" instead of just "what was routed"

### HingeScore calibration infrastructure
- Pool builder (136 prompts), router scorer, bucketing, Markdown reporter — 14 tests
- FEYNMAN_GATE (10 tests): auto-verifies embedded copies match source files
- Pool sync: BLIND_CATEGORIES/V3_PROMPTS/SEMANTIC_PROMPTS were out of sync — fixed
- Zero live changes (pure infrastructure)

### Decision-audit platform — Steps 1-3
- **decisionStore.ts**: localStorage ring buffer (200-entry) capturing full CARDO trace per decision — single-write design
- **DecisionDetail.jsx**: standalone CARDO audit report renderer — 6 CARDO sections with amber headers, router metadata, footer. 13 tests.
- **DecisionFeed.jsx**: list/filter/export UI with domain dropdown, inline expand, CSV/JSON export, per-entry delete, Clear All gate. Integrated into Analytics.jsx tab bar. 10 tests.

### Backend provider timeouts
- 30s `AbortController` on all 4 `callDeepSeek/callGemini/callGroq/callOpenAI` callers
- Prevents hung primary providers from blocking the fallback chain
- Full fallback chain exhausts within ~120s window

**Verification:** 42 suites, 548/548 passing. Build succeeds. Lint 0 errors / 195 warnings.

**Files:** 23 changed, +1,960 / -78 lines.
**Needs Vercel deploy** after merge (timeout fix is in `api/cfai.js`).

items.title: docs(benchmarks): make performance.md the single source of truth; simplify landing pages
items.body:
## Summary
- `README.md`, `docs/index.md`, and `benchmarks/README.md` each hand-maintained their own category-by-category performance table — duplicating numbers that only `docs/performance.md` is auto-generated from. This is the exact class of bug this whole session kept finding (numbers drifting out of sync across files after each fix).
- Replaced all three with a short 2-3 bullet headline + link to `docs/performance.md` for the full breakdown. `benchmarks/README.md` drops its detailed table entirely (most redundant of the three — a "how to run benchmarks" doc, not a results page).
- `docs/performance.md`'s generator now documents the compile-once-evaluate-many methodology for every implementation directly in the generated output (survives regeneration): jsonatapy/jsonata-js already reuse the compiled expression across the timed loop (no further headroom), jsonata-python's benchmark uses its documented `Context` object rather than `transform()`.
- Regenerated `docs/performance.md` and all three results PNGs from a fresh clean release-benchmark CI run (same `v2.1.6` tag, now including the `Context`-reuse fix from #50) — replacing the stale `transform()`-based numbers #49 published hours earlier.
- Fixed an inconsistency caught in review before commit: three files stated three different "up to Nx" headline ceilings (15x/16x/17x), one of which (17x) wasn't supported by the actual data (max is 15.97x). Unified on ~16x everywhere, and fixed a same-file inconsistency in the `evaluate_with_data` speedup claim (3–16x vs 3–15x) to the correct 3–15x.

## Known limitation (flagging explicitly)
This benchmark run used **Python 3.11**, not the 3.14 bump from #50 — `gh run rerun --job` replays the job graph frozen at the run's *original* dispatch time (before #50 merged) and doesn't re-parse the current workflow file, even though it does check out fresh code via the tag. The 3.14 bump is merged and will apply starting with the next real version release; forcing it in now would require a fresh `workflow_dispatch`, which would re-attempt publishing already-shipped 2.1.6 wheels to PyPI/crates.io (`skip-existing: false` — it would fail, not skip).

Also still unfixed (flagged in #49, now hit a third time): `release.yml`'s tag-creation step silently skips moving the tag if it already exists — this session force-moved `v2.1.6` three separate times to work around it. Not fixed here since `release.yml` is sensitive infrastructure; a deliberate follow-up decision.

## Test plan
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass
- [x] Cross-checked the unified "~16x" and "3-15x" claims against the actual computed data (max individual speedup: String Contains 15.97x; evaluate_with_data range: 3.4x-15x from the CI log)
- [x] Verified all internal links (`docs/performance.md`) still resolve correctly from each simplified page

items.title: docs(benchmark): point the README at results instead of stating them
items.body:
## Description

The benchmark README's `Example results`, `What to optimize`, and `Reference point` sections quoted host-specific numbers from an early seed run (USS, threads, scaling table, sweep/heap/load/fault figures, a fixed host + gateway SHA). Those figures drift out of sync with the committed baseline over time - the prose already disagreed with `benchmark/baseline/ci.json`.

This change makes the README **point to where the results live** rather than restate them:

- `Example results` -> `Reading the results`: directs the reader to the committed baseline (`benchmark/baseline/ci.json`) and the per-run output (`report.md`, `summary.json`, `*.png`, `run_metadata.json`), then describes what each lane reports - without hard-coding absolute numbers. The scaling chart stays as a labelled example.
- `What to optimize`: keeps the three optimization targets and their lane pointers; drops the specific magnitudes (re-run `load`/`fault`/`sweep` for current numbers).
- `Reference point`: points to the host/SHA recorded in `ci.json` and `run_metadata.json` instead of a hard-coded host and SHA.

Net: the method, lane descriptions, and qualitative findings stay; the per-host numbers that go stale are gone.

## Checklist

- [x] Docs-only change; no harness behaviour touched
- [x] No dangling references to the removed `Example results` anchor
- [x] Headings and the scaling chart still render

items.title: feat(tool-support): single source of truth for the tool-comparison tables
items.body:
## Summary

The ferro/mutalyzer/biocommons/hgvs-rs feature-support tables were hand-maintained in three places — `README.md`, `docs/BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md`, and the web help tab (`src/service/web/static/js/main.js`) — and had drifted out of sync with each other and with reality. This replaces all three with a single curated source of truth plus a generator, and refreshes the tables against the tools' actual behavior.

- `docs/tool_support_matrix.json` is the single source of truth: 4 tools × 3 categories (reference types, coordinate types, variant types), each cell a fine-grained `{validate, normalize}` pair (closed enums) with footnotes, per-tool versions, and `last_reviewed` dates.
- `src/tool_support/` (dev-gated) holds the serde types and projection logic (enum → glyph), with unit + golden tests.
- `examples/generate_tool_support_tables.rs` renders the README and BENCHMARK_GUIDE tables (between `<!-- BEGIN/END tool-support -->` markers) and a render-ready web JSON. `--check` mode fails CI on any drift, and is wired into the `test` job alongside the existing generator checks.
- The web help tab now builds its tables at runtime from the generated JSON (served via `include_str!`), instead of hardcoded HTML.
- Governance: CI `--check`, `.github/CODEOWNERS` for the matrix file, and a CONTRIBUTING note.

## Data corrections in this refresh

The cells were adjudicated against the tools' source code (ferro `src/normalize/`, hgvs-rs `normalizer.rs` at v0.20.2):

- **hgvs-rs protein**: `✓` → `✗`. hgvs-rs parses `p.` but its normalizer explicitly returns `Error::ProteinVariant`.
- **ferro** protein, RNA, inversion, repeat, conversion: corrected to full normalization. The prior web table understated ferro as validate-only / unsupported for these.
- **biocommons** protein and intronic: `V/N` → `V` (parses/validates but does not normalize, by design).
- **mutalyzer** protein: now carries the network-only footnote.
- README and BENCHMARK_GUIDE tables are now generated from one source, so they share column order and can no longer disagree.

External-tool cells that were not independently source-verified (ENST; mutalyzer/biocommons/hgvs-rs inversion/repeat/conversion) are carried from the prior table and explicitly marked with a `"carried … not source-verified"` note in the JSON, to be confirmed in a future refresh.

## How to refresh in future

Edit `docs/tool_support_matrix.json`, then run `cargo run --features dev --example generate_tool_support_tables`. CI `--check` enforces that the generated tables stay in sync.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo nextest run --features dev` — new `tool_support` unit + golden tests pass (the 9 `axis_*` failures are pre-existing live-upstream conformance tests, unchanged by this PR)
- [ ] `cargo clippy --features dev --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [ ] `cargo run --features dev --example generate_tool_support_tables -- --check` — exits 0
- [ ] `cargo build --features web-service` — succeeds
- [ ] Manual: open the web Help → "HGVS Support" tab and confirm the three tables render (ferro `V/N` across protein/RNA/inversion/repeat/conversion; hgvs-rs protein `V`)

items.title: release: v4.10.0 (595 tests / 43 modules)
items.body:
## Summary

First real version bump since 4.9.1 (2026-07-10) — 30 new tests, 5 new harness modules, and 2 correctness fixes have been sitting on `main` under `[Unreleased]` with only the description-count string bumped, never the version itself. Moves `CHANGELOG.md`'s `[Unreleased]` content to a dated `[4.10.0]` section, bumps `pyproject.toml`, and syncs every place that cites the package version (`SKILL.md`, `CITATION.cff`, `docs/TEST-INVENTORY.md`, `benchmarks/CHANGELOG.md`).

**Context**: this is intentionally timed to land right before publishing the separate `dgb-v1.0.0` benchmark release — that release's publish event will trigger `publish-pypi.yml` (which fires on *any* published release, unfiltered by tag — a known gap, not fixed here per explicit instruction to skip it) and now has a real new version to successfully upload instead of failing on a duplicate 4.9.1.

Two real bugs found and fixed while doing this:

1. **`mcp_harness.py`'s `HARNESS_CLIENT_INFO` had a hardcoded version string** (`"4.9.1"`, literal) sent in the MCP handshake — would have drifted out of sync with this release too. Now derived from `protocol_tests.version.get_harness_version()`, the same source `cli.py` already uses (issue #5 pattern).

Silently undercounted `agent-security version`'s headline number by exactly 12 (583 shown vs. 595 actual). Fixed, and added `TestRegTestCount.test_cli_total_tests_matches_canonical` so this drift class can't recur silently.

Also folds in the round-35 self-audit fixes and the `benchmarks/README.md` corpus-drift fix from this session, since neither had been versioned yet.

items.title: test(benchmarks): add discovery scaling cases
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a second opt-in benchmark slice: dataset discovery scaling. Follows the same pattern as the affine augmentation harness (#115-#118) -- opt-in only, never part of the normal test suite, no timing gate, no new dependency.

**Questions measured:**
- `discover_images`: how does full recursive traversal + fresh stat + extension filter + global materialization/sort scale with file count?
- `discover_image_mask_pairs`: how does two-sided discovery + extension stripping + grouping + duplicate checks + key-set validation + final sorted pairing scale?

**Dataset structure:** each size builds a temp tree with `dataset/images/` and `dataset/masks/`, each split into exactly 10 shard directories (`shard_00`..`shard_09`), with `sample_NNNNNN.jpg`/`.png` filenames. Sizes: 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 files per side (pairing benchmark uses 2x that many total files). All entries are **zero-byte files** created via `Path.touch()` -- never `cv2.imwrite`/valid images/random arrays -- because `discover_images` finds files by extension only and never opens, decodes, or inspects content; this is documented in both the module docstring and `benchmarks/README.md` as matching the contract exactly, not a shortcut.

**Warm-cache policy:** every timed call is preceded by one untimed, asserted preflight call that validates the dataset and warms the filesystem metadata cache. Both groups are explicitly warm-filesystem-cache measurements; cold-cache traversal is out of scope (OS/filesystem/disk/machine-state dependent, no purge/sync mechanism here).

**No raw baseline:** unlike the affine family's raw/`improcv` pairing, there is no `os.walk`/`Path.rglob`/`glob`/manual-pairing comparison. `discover_images`'s contract (fresh per-entry stat, symlink/reparse-point skipping, hidden-file policy, deterministic global sort, extension normalization) and `discover_image_mask_pairs`'s strict bijection have no raw equivalent of matching strength -- this slice measures the public API's own scaling, not a ratio against a semantically weaker iterator.

**Groups:** `discovery-images` (3 cases) and `discovery-pairs` (3 cases) -- real `pytest-benchmark` groups, 6 benchmark entries total.

**Explicitly out of scope for this PR:** no baseline JSON committed (a first stats-only discovery baseline follows in a separate PR from a clean, final harness SHA), no failure-path benchmarks (unmatched/duplicate/hidden/symlink/permission/etc. stay covered by correctness tests only), no cold-cache benchmark, no custom-extension benchmark, no raw comparison, no API/dependency/version/CI changes.

## Verification performed

- Normal suite: `uv run pytest` -> **4191 passed, 6 skipped** (unchanged; `benchmarks/` stays outside `testpaths`).
- Full benchmark smoke: `uv run --group benchmark pytest benchmarks/ --benchmark-disable` -> **26 passed** (20 affine + 6 new discovery) in ~5.4s.
- Short functional run (`--benchmark-warmup=on --benchmark-min-rounds=2 --benchmark-max-time=0.05`, discovery file only): 6 entries, groups 3/3, `rounds >= 2` throughout, `extra_info` present for all. Medians increased monotonically with size in both groups on this machine/run (not published as a baseline, confirmation only):
  - `discovery-images`: ~2.25ms -> ~22.7ms -> ~226ms
  - `discovery-pairs`: ~8.2ms -> ~82.6ms -> ~856ms
- Stats-only JSON smoke (`--benchmark-storage`/`--benchmark-save`, written to `/tmp`, never copied into the repo): 6 entries, groups `discovery-images:3` / `discovery-pairs:3`, `stats.data` confirmed **absent**, `median`/`mean`/`stddev`/`iqr`/`rounds`/`iterations`/`params`/`extra_info` all present, `machine_info`/`commit_info` present, no absolute temp paths found in the file (13,585 bytes total).
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` / `pyright`: all clean.
- Build + packaging: `uv build` + `twine check` both PASSED; wheel excludes `benchmarks/` entirely; sdist includes the new `benchmark_discovery.py` alongside existing benchmark content, no new discovery JSON. sdist size 2,118,646 bytes vs. 2,114,117 bytes on `main` (+4,529 bytes, consistent with just the new source file).
- Final diff before commit: `M CHANGELOG.md`, `M benchmarks/README.md`, `?? benchmarks/benchmark_discovery.py` -- exactly as scoped, nothing else touched.

items.title: test(bench): performance-regression harness with committed targets, wired into CI (#263)
items.body:
Closes #263

Wires resdag's internal fast-path speedups to a committed, CI-gated
performance-regression harness so the headline speed claims can't silently rot.

## What changed

- **`benchmarks/targets.json`** — committed floors per (context, metric) cell.
  - `internal_ratios`: the **hard gate** — hardware-portable CPU A/B ratios
    (resdag's fast path vs its own naive path, no external libraries). Each cell
    carries an `enforced_min_ratio` (gated) and an `aspirational_ratio`
    (audit/GPU headline, documented but not enforced).
  - `external_floors`: **informational only** — cross-library numbers
    transcribed from `benchmarks/results/REPORT.md` (2026-06-14). Never asserted,
    because reservoirpy / ReservoirComputing.jl may be absent.
- **`tests/test_benchmarks/test_perf_regression.py`** — `benchmark`-marked test
  that reads `targets.json` and asserts three internal ratios, each with a
  numerical-correctness check against its naive twin:
  | Ratio | Floor | Ticket |
  |---|---|---|
  | flat forecast vs per-step graph re-execution | ≥ 1.8× | #254 |
  | vectorized NG-RC vs per-step scan | ≥ 5× | #255 |
  | fast spectral radius vs dense eigvals | ≥ 2× | #185 |
  Interleaved best-of-N A/B timing + a small-reservoir config keep the
  flat-engine gate robust on contended runners. A plain (non-benchmark) test
  guards the targets-file shape so the normal lane catches malformed/out-of-sync
  targets.
- **`benchmarks/rc_bench/run.py`** — new `--report` flag renders `REPORT.md` in
  the same deterministic run-and-render step.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — benchmark lane now also triggers on the
  **`benchmark`** PR label (in addition to nightly schedule + manual dispatch),
  gates on `targets.json` across both `tests/test_benchmarks` and
  `tests/test_performance`, and re-renders + uploads `REPORT.md` as an artifact.
  `release.yml` is untouched; releases stay disabled.
- **`benchmarks/README.md`** — documents the regression gate, the floors table,
  the local command, and the CI lane.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `benchmarks/targets.json` defines floor numbers/ratios per (context, metric) cell from `REPORT.md` and this audit.
- [x] A benchmark-marked test asserts hardware-portable internal speedup ratios and fails on regression.
- [x] CI runs the smoke matrix on schedule / PR-label and uploads `REPORT.md`; documented in `benchmarks/README.md`.
- [x] Re-running the report regenerates `REPORT.md` deterministically with the flat-engine forecast win reflected.

## Notes

- The gating test asserts only **internal** ratios — runnable on CPU with no
  external library. External-library floor numbers live in `external_floors` as
  informational records pulled from `REPORT.md`; they are never asserted.
- CPU rows and the precision (VPT) metrics are seed-deterministic; only the
  `resdag-gpu` row carries run-to-run CUDA floating-point jitter, so the
  committed `REPORT.md` snapshot is left as the canonical cross-library record.

## Verification

- `pytest -m benchmark tests/test_benchmarks` — 3 passed (stable across repeated runs)
- affected-tests full suite — 1899 passed, 3 skipped, 9 deselected (benchmark)
- `ruff check src tests` — clean · `black --check src tests` — clean · `mypy src` — no issues

items.title: cmake: drop FPSAN_ENABLE_HIP; predicate the HIP build on CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER
items.body:
FPSAN_ENABLE_HIP was a derived cache option layered on top of CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER, and a cached option carries its own footgun: once initialized it lingers as build-dir state that can drift out of sync with the toolchain that's actually present. Remove it entirely and make CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER the single source of truth -- tests/examples/benchmarks compile as HIP whenever a HIP compiler is available (if(CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER)) and as pure C++ otherwise.

To keep the documented "pure C++ even on a HIP box" build, force-off is now an explicit empty compiler: -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=. The ROCM_PATH auto-derivation only fires when CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER is *undefined* (so an explicit value -- empty or not -- is respected), and check_language(HIP) is skipped when it is defined-but-empty, so nothing resurrects a forced-off compiler.

Updated tests/, examples/, benchmarks/ gates, the top-level option doc, README, and docs/python.md (HIP recipes drop -DFPSAN_ENABLE_HIP=ON; pure-C++ recipes use -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=).

Verified: compiler+arch -> HIP enabled (no enable flag); -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=
+ arch -> host build (force-off honored); clean CPU build 448/448, host-only (349 vs the HIP build's 744 registered tests).

items.title: Implement missing baselines and evaluation harnesses from supervisor review (S2/S3/A3/A5/S4)
items.body:
## Summary

The supervisor review letter's items (B1–B4, S1–S6, G1–G14, A1–A6) all map to rows already logged as "Done" in `docs/supervisor_feedback_log.md` and resolved in the Concept Note v3.0/v4.0 documentation. Re-verifying against the actual codebase found the gap was purely between docs and code — several deliverables the docs claimed were implemented did not actually exist. This PR closes that gap:

- **`agents/pdqn_agent.py`, `agents/mpdqn_agent.py`** (S2) — flat (non-branching) baselines over the 2^R joint RRH-activation space, single critic (no twin), reusing the proposed method's `SharedEncoder`/`ContinuousParameterNetwork` for a fair comparison. P-DQN uses a single unmasked pass (the documented "false gradient" cross-talk); MP-DQN adds genuine multi-pass masking, verified by a dedicated unit test that perturbing a masked-out RRH's parameters does not change that action's Q-value. Both are guarded against R>20 with an explicit error instead of a silent OOM at R=35/50 — the scaling failure is itself part of the documented case for branching (§10.3.1/B3).
- **`agents/ddpg_agent.py`** (RQ3) — pure-DDPG continuous-relaxation baseline: the actor outputs a continuous "soft" RRH-activation gate that is thresholded only at execution time, matching the original v1.0 concept note's design.
- **`evaluation/csi_robustness.py`** (S3) — perturbs only the channel-gain slice of the *observation* fed to a frozen trained policy (sigma in {0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1}), leaving the environment's true physics/reward computation untouched, per §12.5's "evaluation-only, no retraining" spec.
- **`evaluation/generalization.py`** (A5/G13) + a new `weekend_suburban` traffic profile in `cran_env/traffic_model.py` — trains once on the default weekday/urban profile and evaluates zero-shot on the weekend/suburban variant.
- **`evaluation/latency_benchmark.py`** (A3/G14) — isolated forward-pass latency at R = 5, 12, 20, 35, 50 (matching §12.3's exact sweep), explicitly skipping P-DQN/MP-DQN above their tractable range rather than crashing.
- **`evaluation/convergence.py`** — added `compute_cohens_d()` (S4/G11). While wiring it in, found and fixed a real bug: the module's proposed-method lookup was still the hardcoded, superseded string `"Hybrid_SAC_DDQN"`, but `training/train_hybrid.py` actually saves `"Branching_MP_DQN"` — every paired statistical comparison against the real proposed method was silently comparing against an empty placeholder array. The same stale-name bug existed in `evaluation/scalability.py`'s result dict key; both fixed.
- **`training/train_baselines.py`** — wired `ddpg`/`pdqn`/`mpdqn` into the unified 9-method benchmark runner.
- **`AGENTS.md`, `docs/workflow.md`, `README.md`, `docs/supervisor_feedback_log.md`** — synced status trackers to what's now actually implemented vs. still pending a full-scale (10-seed, thesis-scale) experiment run.

## Out of scope / not claimed as done

No full-scale experiments have been run — everything above is implemented and unit-tested at small network sizes only. The actual 10-seed × 9-method comparison, CSI-robustness curve, generalization result, and latency benchmark at thesis scale still need to be executed before Chapter 4 can be written.

## Test plan

- [x] All 44 tests pass (`python -m pytest tests/ -q`): 36 pre-existing + 8 new (`tests/test_new_baselines.py`, `tests/test_new_evaluations.py`)
- [x] Dedicated correctness test confirms MP-DQN's masking actually zeroes out irrelevant RRH parameters (`test_mpdqn_masks_inactive_rrh_params`)
- [x] Dedicated regression test guards against the proposed-method name drifting out of sync again (`test_analyze_convergence_with_mock_results`)
- [x] `training/train_baselines.py` integration test confirms `ddpg`/`pdqn`/`mpdqn` run end-to-end through the shared benchmark runner
- [ ] Full-scale (10-seed) experiment run — not part of this PR

items.title: Voice stack: streaming STT, distilled router, and speech-to-speech (A/B/C)
items.body:
Large branch evolving Gia's voice stack end to end — latency, routing, and a second (speech-to-speech) architecture — plus the supporting fixes and a docs restructure. **58 commits, 224 files (+26k/−3.8k); 472 tests pass.**

## Highlights

**Speech-to-speech voice mode (new).** A realtime path on `gpt-realtime` alongside the decomposed pipeline, behind `VOICE_MODE`, sharing memory/Spotify/Brave + workers:
- `providers/realtime.py` — `RealtimeSession` bridge + DI'd tool dispatch
- `api/voice_realtime.py` — `WS /voice/realtime`
- frontend `realtimeSession.ts` + `realtimePlayer.ts`, `useVoiceSession` branch
- `REALTIME_VOICE_SOURCE` toggles **model voice (B)** vs **ElevenLabs (C)** — graceful fallback when ElevenLabs is down
- model-acknowledges-then-searches to mask tool latency; per-turn Langfuse tracing

**Latency.** Streaming STT (Deepgram Flux) with mid-utterance router **prewarm**; speculative reply + Spotify search; **sentence-streaming TTS** on both paths; **four-tier router cascade** with a distilled MiniLM + scikit-learn classifier (~40–60 ms vs ~1.1–1.7 s LLM). Result: chat TTFA ~4–6 s (pipeline) → ~1.0–1.1 s (realtime). Full A/B/C comparison in `docs/benchmarks.md`.

**Faster Spotify search.** Direct Web API (pooled, cached token) with MCP fallback — **~0.4 s warm vs ~1.9 s**; token prewarmed at startup; the MCP client routes through it so the pipeline benefits too.

**Removed, deliberately.** CrewAI (custom asyncio orchestration instead) and Spotify's deprecated audio-features machinery (queueing rebuilt on stated order / search relevance; mood rebuilt as LLM labels over a closed vocabulary).

## Fixes
- `mood.py` missing `PromptRegistry`/`get_registry`/`get_fast_llm`/`AGENT_KEY` — a CrewAI-removal regression that made the app un-importable
- `uv.lock` out of sync with `pyproject` (missing `litellm`) → api container crash-looped on `ModuleNotFoundError`; regenerated
- realtime WS endpoint used HTTP request-scoped deps; now reads `app.state` directly

## Docs
Split the dense README into a lean `README.md` + `docs/` (`architecture`, `latency`, `benchmarks`, `memory`, `design`).

## Notes for review
- Realtime is validated against the live OpenAI Realtime API + a mocked socket; full in-browser TTFA and cross-browser playback are pending.
- Off-by-default flags: distilled router (`router_local_enabled`), CrewAI curator, rerank.

items.title: Cleanup: chase drift, dead code, and a batch-distinctness gap after the recent spikes
items.body:
## Why

Several spikes merged to `main` in close succession — D24/D25 (large capped minis), D26 (agent solver), D27/D28 (Gibbs layout field) — alongside a mid-stream decision *renumbering*. The automated gate (ruff / mypy / import-linter / pytest) stayed green throughout, which is exactly the blind spot: it catches layering, types, and broken invariants, but not *semantic* drift. So prose, code comments, and a little dead surface fell out of sync with the code. This PR chases the three classes down. It changes no engine, invariant, or layer; the full gate stays green. Recorded as **D29**.

Three audit passes (dead code, doc↔code drift, architecture violations the linters can't see) drove the work.

## Dead code removed

- `Lexicon.is_word` — zero callers anywhere in `src`/`scripts`/`tests`.
- `CapturingWriter` — referenced only in docstrings; the one test that needs a recording sink rolls its own inline `Writer`.

Both are one `git show` away per the D19 discipline. Deliberately **kept** despite looking caller-light: the static-difficulty subsystem (`analyze`, `CrossingOpenness`/`StructuralDifficulty`, `Lexicon.n_letters_at`, D21 A′) and the Gibbs `reject_reason`/`anneal_field` study instruments (D28) — both are load-bearing benchmark surface the docs describe as built and the tests exercise.

## Correctness: batch-wide distinctness

`MiniService.generate` deduped emitted grids only on the difficulty-*targeting* path. The plain path could return the same fill twice, because a *complete* backtracker yields the same solution under different seeds when the band admits few (e.g. `mini 5 90 3` at a tight bar). Per-grid distinctness (invariant 3) was never at risk — `backtrack`/`validate` still enforce 2N distinct words; this is invariant 3 applied **grid-wide across the batch**, which the tool's "distinct minis" wording promises. The `seen`-set guard is hoisted to cover every emitted grid, pinned by a regression test. Single-grid reproducibility is unchanged (`mini 5 70 1` byte-identical; verified).

## Stale in-code references

The difficulty spike was renumbered (D20/D21/D22 → D21/D22/D23 once D20 "the whole-puzzle path" was inserted), but comments in `app/difficulty.py`, `app/ports.py`, and `scripts/difficulty.py` still cited the old numbers — repointed to D21 (decomposition) / D22 (solve order). Also tightened `fill_capped_once`'s docstring: it always runs the layout search under a node budget, so its `None` is budget exhaustion, never a UNSAT theorem (the unbudgeted proof is `capped_layout_exists`).

## Docs re-synced to the code

- **architecture.md**: fix the stale "`generate.py` is the demo/property-check" claim (it's a shim; the check moved to `tests/test_patterns.py`, as the same file already said elsewhere); restore `core/` + `core/engines/` prefixes to five section headers left over from the reorg; add `solve_effort.py` to the driver list.
- **CLAUDE.md**: decision-log range `D1–D13` → `D1–D28`; drop the removed `CapturingWriter`; list the full benchmark-driver set.
- **README**: the status ledger still called clue generation "not started" despite the shipped clue (D15/D16/D20), difficulty (D21–D23), and agent-solve (D26) work — added those, and surfaced the `puzzle`/`solve` tools in the layout/run sections.
- **notes.md**: framed the initial-spike status snapshot as historical (its `from_scored_file` claim moved to the `FileLexicon` adapter at D14).
- **decisions.md**: recorded the cleanup as **D29**.

## Verification

All five gate commands green (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`, `lint-imports`, `pytest` — +1 test). Smoke-tested `mini`, `generate --max-len`, and `demo`; confirmed `mini 5 70 1` output is byte-identical and a high-bar batch (`mini 5 90 5`) is duplicate-free.

items.title: feat(learn): promote the min-chars audit to its own step with an inspectable trace
items.body:
## Summary

The `learn` skill's "minimum viable rule text" audit was narrated in prose inside Step 5 and left no artifact, so a skipped audit was indistinguishable from a light one — the failure mode both #211 and #217 describe. This promotes it to its own numbered step and makes it emit an inspectable trace.

- **`### 5. Audit Rule Text`** is now its own step, with the downstream steps renumbered 5→6, 6→7, 7→8. It names the split procedure (sentence and em-dash boundaries), the four things a fragment may contribute, and what fails the check. Its second paragraph carries #217's falsifiable self-check: *"If the user has to ask whether a draft is minimal, the audit was skipped, not just light."*
- **A `Cut in audit:` field in the plan template**, so the audit's result is shown to the user *before* any file write — either the clauses cut, or `none` plus a one-word defense per kept clause. This is the inspectable artifact; a skipped audit is now visible at the confirmation gate.
- **11 structural pytest tests** (`tests/learn/test_audit_trace.py`) that parse the real `SKILL.md` and fail on renumbering drift, a missing audit step, or the template field moving out of the plan block.

Skill version `1.2` → `1.3`. Closes #211. Closes #217 (its wording is folded into the new step rather than applied to the old paragraph — see below).

## This delivers transparency, not concision — and the eval says so

**The original acceptance target was not met, and the change ships anyway on a narrower claim.** Reviewers should read `evals/learn/benchmark.md` before this PR body.

`plan.md`'s target was that eval 9's `turn1-rule-under-200-chars` assertion would flip to pass. It did not. A same-model v1.2-vs-v1.3 control shows why:

| Model | v1.2 | v1.3 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-sonnet-5` | 239 chars | 243 chars | **+4 (longer)** |
| `claude-opus-5` | 264 chars | 270 chars | **+6 (longer)** |

v1.2 already ran a min-chars audit — v1.3 *formalized an existing behavior rather than introducing one*, so rule length did not move. The audit fires and is well-formed but does not bite. **The 200-char threshold and the assertion wording were deliberately left unchanged rather than loosened to fit the result.**

What did work: **`plan-shows-cut-in-audit` is fully discriminating** — both `with_skill` runs emitted the field; neither `without_skill` run showed a plan at all. Eval 9 goes 5/6 `with_skill` on both models vs 2/6 and 3/6 baseline. That is a real gain in transparency; it is not the gain the acceptance criterion measures.

There is also a **directional turn-2 regression** worth a reviewer's eye: at v1.2 the second turn found further cuts (239→224, 264→**218**); at v1.3 both models replied `already minimal` and cut nothing. The 218-char cell is the closest any observed run has come to the 200-char target — and it came from the version *without* this change. Sample size is one run per cell, so this is directional, not conclusive. Tracked in #224.

**The last commit is the skill auditing itself.** `0c5d34d` came from running `/learn` at v1.3 on this PR's own review cycle — four `CLAUDE.md` rules, each carrying its `Cut in audit:` trace. Worth knowing how that went: the emitted traces were specific and confident, and the reviewer's reply was verbatim the phrase the step's own self-check names — *"is this the min chars needed?"* Re-auditing on that prompt cut substantially more from all four rules, none of it requiring information unavailable on the first pass. Recorded on #224 as a third data point.

That is the transparency claim holding and the concision claim failing, in one commit: without the `Cut in audit:` lines there would have been nothing to interrogate, and the audit still did not bite until a human asked. It is not an argument for strengthening the step's wording — emphatic wording is the intervention #217 proposed and #211 rejected on eval evidence, and the emphatic line already in the file is the one that failed. A shape change (making the trace provisional rather than a settled verdict) is the v1.4 candidate worth measuring.

## Measurement caveat

Claude 4.6/4.7 were unreachable from the eval harness, so the v1.3 eval-9 runs are on `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-opus-5` and are labeled as such. Evals 0-5, 7, 8 remain at v1.0 on 4.6/4.7 (there is no eval 6 — the suite skips that ID, so "evals 0-8" was never an accurate range and has been corrected repo-wide in this PR). **Do not read 209 → 243 as a regression caused by v1.3** — that comparison spans model generations. The v1.2 control runs exist precisely to break that confound; they live in `benchmark.json` `notes[4]`, not in the `runs` array, so they cannot contaminate `run_summary`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/learn/` — 11 new tests pass
- [ ] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/` — full suite, 1310 passed
- [ ] `rg -c '^### [0-9]+\. [A-Z]' skills/learn/SKILL.md` → `8` (gapless 1–8; the bare `[0-9]+\.` form matches the fenced Route C template too and would pass for the wrong reason)
- [ ] `rg -n 'Step 5 confirmation' skills/learn/` → no hits (cross-reference updated to Step 6)
- [ ] `python3 -c 'import json; json.load(open("evals/learn/benchmark.json"))'` → valid, and 0 non-ASCII bytes
- [ ] `npx cspell "skills/**/*.md" "specs/**/*.md"` → clean

## Review notes

Reviewed by a whole-branch pass that caught one Important finding, now fixed in `51d259e`: a `benchmark.json` run note attributed 308 → 270 to the audit step, which both spans model generations and runs opposite to the control. Four Minor test-tightening findings were triaged as deferrable; the most useful to know is that the em-dash assertion guards the literal word `"em-dash"`, not the split semantics.

Five subsequent bot-review rounds produced four more commits, none of which change skill behavior:

- `96d6ece` — `evals 0-8` named an eval 6 that does not exist. Corrected in `README.md`, `benchmark.md`, and `benchmark.json`, which was already self-contradicting (`8 evals (0-5, 7, 8)` in one note, `evals 0-8` in 20 others). Fixing only the Markdown would have left drift in the file the repo treats as authoritative over prose.
- `1efccbd` — the removal test anchored on `the audit is not optional`, a phrase generic enough to reappear legitimately. Re-anchored on the removed paragraph's distinctive opener, verified red at `08bd629` and green at HEAD. (`Before showing the plan` is *not* usable — it still opens the dedup sentence in Present Plan.)
- `f9ad11d` — `tasks.md` had fallen out of sync with the committed test and named executors the runner can no longer reach.
- `7be796f` — `benchmark.json`'s top-level metadata read as one tuple (`claude-opus-4-7`, v1.3, 2026-07-30) describing no run in the file. Each `models_tested[]` entry now carries its own `skill_version`, the shape `evals/pr-human-guide/benchmark.json` uses. Reverting `metadata.skill_version` instead would violate `evals/CLAUDE.md`, which requires it to track the current skill version when new runs are added.

items.title: docs: documentation overhaul — improvement backlog, README polish, staleness fixes
items.body:
## What this is

A documentation-only overhaul. I surveyed the full codebase and all active docs, identified what makes Tank World genuinely special, captured a prioritized improvement plan, and fixed documentation that had drifted out of sync with the code. No code changes, no test risk.

## The most interesting aspects (now documented as "crown jewels")

1. **Git as the heredity mechanism** — the `benchmarks/ → champions/ → validate_improvement.py → CI` loop turns "the number went up" into a reproducible scientific claim.
2. **Composable behaviors over black boxes** — fish behavior factors into four orthogonal, genetically-tuned dimensions; interpretable and evolvable.
3. **Determinism as a first-class invariant** — seeded RNG everywhere, record/replay, double-run CI checks.
4. **A full Texas Hold'em engine with CFR learning inside an ALife sim** — fish play poker for energy and inherit learned regret tables.
5. **Multi-world backend** — one evolutionary core renders as fish tank, petri dish, or soccer pitch.

## Changes

**New**
- `docs/IMPROVEMENT_PROPOSALS.md` — a living, prioritized engineering backlog. Names the crown jewels (so we protect them) then gives concrete, effort/impact-tagged implementation plans across five themes: hardening the evolution loop, taming the god files, consolidating the algorithm library, developer/observer experience, and docs that sell the project.
- `docs/archive/README.md` — a retention/deprecation policy so the ~43 archived docs stop sitting beside active ones without context.

**README**
- Added CI / benchmark / Python / license / black badges.
- Replaced the ASCII evolution-loop and three-layer descriptions with rendered **Mermaid diagrams** (hardened to avoid `&` in labels for cross-renderer safety).
- Linked the new proposals doc.

**Staleness fixes (all verified against code)**
- `docs/BEHAVIOR_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md`: algorithm count 48 → 58 with the real per-category breakdown (checked against `core/algorithms/registry.py`).
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`: marked `validate_improvement.py` and `bench.yml` as shipped (they exist); clarified which tank benchmarks are live vs. planned; bumped last-updated date.
- `docs/INDEX.md`: added the previously-missing `REPLAY.md` / `UI_SPEC.md` entries and the proposals doc.
- `scripts/README.md`: expanded from a partial list to a grouped reference of the evolution-loop, analysis, diagnosis, profiling, and verification scripts (every entry verified to exist).

## Follow-ups (tracked in the new proposals doc, not in this PR)

The highest-impact "fun to use" items are code, and belong in a focused follow-up PR:
- `scripts/diagnose.py` — one-command environment health check (S / ★★★)
- one-command startup (S / ★★★)
- generated algorithm catalog so code-mirroring docs can't drift again (the anti-drift fix for the 48-vs-58 bug)

## Verification

- Every referenced file/command confirmed present.
- Algorithm count checked against the registry (`len(ALL_ALGORITHMS) == 58`).
- Mermaid diagrams reviewed for valid syntax.
- pre-commit hooks pass (docs-only; Python checks skipped as no `.py` changed).

items.title: feat: run_kaggle_validation -- train the AllGraph on an arbitrary Kaggle dataset
items.body:
## Context

Every existing entry point trains on a **curated** dataset: `run_standard_validation.py` iterates the shared registry, where each entry is a hand-written `loader(reduced, device) -> {train, test, task, chance, field, sota}` that already knows its target column, its split, and its SOTA reference. There was no path for a dataset the project has never seen — no `kagglehub`, no pandas CSV ingest, no image-folder reader.

The gap is **ingestion, not modelling**. Once data is an `AllData`, routing, priced selection, training, evaluation, the skill axis, and the merge-on-write results store are already generic. So this adds one script that turns a Kaggle handle into an `AllData` pair and hands off to the existing pipeline verbatim.

The README sections describing this runner already landed in #10; this PR is the script they describe.

## What it does

Imports `add_pipeline_args` / `resolve_pipeline` / `apply_opt_preset` / `make_allgraph` / `_eval_test` / `record_row` from `run_standard_validation` rather than re-implementing any of it, so a Kaggle run is configured identically to a benchmark run and takes all 40 shared flags.

Three auto-detected ingest modes:

| mode | path | contract |
|---|---|---|
| `tabular` | CSV/TSV/parquet → numeric + one-hot matrix | rank 2 → `sequence` |
| `images` | class-dir tree / train-test dirs / flat dir + labels CSV → `(N,C,hw,hw)` | rank 4 → `spatial` |
| `npy` | `.npy`/`.npz` → rank passed through | rank 2–6 → grid-rank router |

```bash
pip install "ilmarinen[kaggle]"
python validation_runners/run_kaggle_validation.py --handle uciml/iris --inspect
python validation_runners/run_kaggle_validation.py --handle uciml/iris --epochs 40
python validation_runners/run_kaggle_validation.py --local_dir /path/to/extracted   # offline
```

**`--inspect` is the intended first step** against an unfamiliar handle: file inventory, detected mode, a per-column profile carrying the verdict the encoder will apply, target/task guesses, split, chance, routed contract, budget — and it trains nothing. It reaches those answers by running the *real* ingest on a capped subset, so there is no second preview implementation to drift out of sync.

## Correctness decisions worth reviewing

- **Leakage discipline.** The split is drawn first; every statistic (imputation median, z-score mean/std, one-hot level set, label map, per-channel image stats) is fit on the **train rows only**; a category seen only at test encodes to an all-zero block. This deliberately differs from `core/extended_datasets.py:load_superconductivity`, which z-scores the whole dataset before splitting. Pinned by `test_scaler_is_fit_on_train_only`.
- **`chance` is the train-majority predictor scored on the test split** — not `1/K`, not the test majority rate, both of which flatter a model on an imbalanced target. Pinned by `test_chance_is_train_majority_scored_on_test`.
- **Budget.** Unlike the standard runner this one takes `--width/--depth/--epochs`, since no tuned budget exists for an unseen dataset. Left unset it routes *without training* (an `AllGraph.route` probe) and reads that contract's entry from the same `BUDGET` table; `--epochs_scale` still multiplies. The probe replays the `--enabled_contracts` restriction, which `route()` does not apply but `fit()` does.
- **Separate results file.** Rows go to `<data-dir>/kaggle_val_rows.json`, never `standard_val_rows.json` — that file is what `make_results_table --insert-readme` renders into the published benchmark table. A test asserts the runner never names it.
- **Corrupt-image alignment.** `load_images` returns the *kept indices*, not a count, so a truncated JPEG drops its own label rather than shifting every later label by one.

## Drive-by fix

`python -m validation_runners.<name>` was documented in both READMEs but raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'run_standard_validation'` — under `-m`, `sys.path[0]` is the CWD rather than the script's directory, so the sibling import never resolved. Two lines added to `run_quick_validation.py` and `run_cellpainting_validation.py`; all five runners now respond to the documented form.

## Dependencies

`kagglehub` / `pandas` / `pillow` become a new **optional** `kaggle` extra, imported lazily per mode, so nothing in the rest of the package gains a dependency. The `>=0.3.10` kagglehub floor rather than `>=1.0` because the `*_download` signatures are identical across 0.3.x and 1.x.

## Tests

`tests_unit/test_kaggle_validation.py` — 76 cases, **fully offline** via `--local_dir` (one test installs a `kagglehub` stub that raises on any attribute access, proving the offline path never reaches it). `pandas`/`Pillow` are `importorskip`-guarded since CI installs neither, so the required `unit tests` check is unaffected. Four `smoke`-marked end-to-end cases.

## Verification

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean (161 files)
- `pytest tests_unit/ -m "not smoke"` → **318 passed, 1 skipped**
- `pytest tests_unit/ -m smoke` → **85 passed**
- All five runners respond to `python -m validation_runners.<name> --help`
- End-to-end on synthetic fixtures, all three modes: tabular → `sequence` acc 0.875 vs chance 0.525 (skill +0.737); images → `spatial` acc 1.000 (skill +1.000); npz regression → `MAE[target]` with R² 0.706 — all three upserted into one results document

## Honest framing

Stated in the module docstring and both READMEs: a flat tabular feature vector routes to the `sequence` contract and is read as `(n, T=n_features, C=1)`. ilmarinen is a meta-optimizer over computational contracts, not a tabular specialist — **expect to lose to gradient boosting on tabular Kaggle data**. The value is watching routing and priced selection behave on data nobody tuned them for. The docstring lists ten such caveats, including that this is not a leaderboard score (the split is ours, not the competition's hidden test set).

items.title: Auto-detect TornadoVM backend in llama-tornado / llamaTornado

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

items.body:
### Description
  
 This PR enables the automatic detection of the sdk, so users do not need to use the `opencl`/`--ptx`/`--cuda`/`--metal` flags from `llama-tornado` and `llamaTornado`. 

  The backend is now auto-detected from the installed TornadoVM SDK (`$TORNADOVM_HOME/etc/tornado.backend`, which the TornadoVM installer already writes, e.g. `tornado.backends=cuda-backend`), so the same command works unmodified against  any single-backend SDK - `5.1.0-jdk25-opencl`, `-ptx`, `-cuda`, or `-metal`.
  
  If an SDK bundles more than one backend, priority order `cuda > ptx > opencl > metal`  picks one. If users need to use a lower priority backend, they can still use the `opencl`/`--ptx`/`--cuda`/`--metal` flags from `llama-tornado` and `llamaTornado`.

Both scripts print which backend they picked, e.g.:  Detected TornadoVM backend: cuda (from .../etc/tornado.backend).

 ### Why                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                           
  Backend selection was a manual flag that had to match whatever SDK happened to be on  `TORNADOVM_HOME` — easy to get out of sync (wrong flag against a single-backend SDK                                 silently produces confusing failures downstream). Since the SDK itself already records          which backend(s) it was built with, the launcher can just read that instead of asking the user to repeat it.                          

The existing flags are becoming optional, and remain as a way that users can explicitly ask for a backend in case an SDK bundles multiple backends.                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                           
   ### Compatibility                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                           
  - Passing an old flag still works as long as it is defined in the used SDK (TORNADOVM_HOME/etc/tornado.backend`).                                                                                                                        
  - `llamaTornado` (Java) was missing a `CUDA` backend case entirely (only had        `OPENCL`/`PTX`/`METAL`), so it couldn't previously build a working command against a     CUDA-backend SDK at all. Added, mirroring `llama-tornado`.                                                                                                             
  - Verified against the `--bench`/`--server` features merged in from `main` in the                  meantime — both still resolve the backend before dispatching to `LlamaBench`/       `OpenAIServer`/`LlamaApp`, no flag collisions. Found and fixed 3 README examples for                           those features that used the now-removed `--cuda` flag (would have errored if                                                                                    copy-pasted), and refreshed the stale `--help` dump.                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                           
  ### Where                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                           
  - `llama-tornado`, `llamaTornado` — the actual auto-detection + CUDA support                                                                                             
  - `.github/workflows/build-and-run.yml`, `.github/actions/run-inference/action.yml` -        drop now-redundant `--<backend>` flags (each CI matrix leg already builds and points      `TORNADOVM_HOME` at a single-backend SDK)                                                                                                                              
  - `scripts/benchmark_backends.sh`, `scripts/all.sh` - same                                                                                                               
  - `README.md`, `.claude/skills/build-n-run-engine/SKILL.md`,        `.claude/agents/gpullama-benchmarking-specialist.md` - docs 


### How to test                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                           
  1. Point `TORNADOVM_HOME` at any single-backend TornadoVM SDK (`source ./set_paths` or  equivalent) and confirm `$TORNADOVM_HOME/etc/tornado.backend` exists.                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                           
  2. Auto-detection + correct backend wiring:                                                                                                                              
```bash
./llama-tornado --model <path.gguf> --show-command                                                                                                                    
./llamaTornado  --model <path.gguf> --show-command                                              
```

Both should print Detected TornadoVM backend: <backend> (from .../tornado.backend)                             and the printed java command should reference that backend's                             exportLists/<backend>-exports and tornado.drivers.<backend> module.                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                           
  3. Changed backend flag guard to be optional (for multi-backend bundled SDKs):    
```bash
./llama-tornado --model <path.gguf> --cuda                                                                                                                               
./llamaTornado  --model <path.gguf> --ptx                          
```                     

For example on M4 with OpenCL and Metal:

```bash
./llama-tornado --model /opt/models/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-F16.gguf --gpu --metal                
Detected TornadoVM backends: opencl, metal (from /Users/thanos/repositories/TornadoVM/dist/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-metal-opencl-mac-aarch64/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-metal-opencl/etc/tornado.backend) - using metal (requested via --metal)
```      
                                                                                                                                              
  4. New features still compose correctly with detection:                                                                                                                  
```bash  
./llama-tornado --model <path.gguf> --bench --bench-args "-p 512 -n 128" --show-command                                                                                  
./llama-tornado --model <path.gguf> --server --port 8080 --show-command                                                                                                  
./llamaTornado  --model <path.gguf> --bench --bench-args "-p 512 -n 128" --show-command         
```      
                                                                   
Command should target bench.LlamaBench / server.OpenAIServer respectively, still        with the correct backend's exports/modules.
  5. Real end-to-end run (drop --show-command, or add --execute-after-show) against an       actual GGUF model, to confirm the JVM actually starts and TornadoVM initializes on       the detected backend.                                                                                                                                                    
  6. If SDKs for more than one backend are available, repeat step 2 against each to       confirm detection tracks whichever TORNADOVM_HOME is currently set, with no stale  state between runs.                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                           
  Repo CI (build-and-run.yml) exercises the opencl/ptx/cuda matrix end-to-end on push,        which is the main regression check for backend wiring across all three. 
  
  ### Test with SDKs that contain multiple backends

Use the full option from SDKMAN!, or if you do not have SPIR-V build with at least two backends:
```bash
sdk install tornadovm 5.1.0-jdk25-full
```

or

```bash
cd TornadoVM
make BACKEND=opencl,cuda sdk && source setvars.sh
```

Then go to root directory of GPULlama3 and build the project.

```bash
./mvnw clean install
./llama-tornado --gpu --model /opt/models/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf 
```

and it dumps a message when multiple backends are available, the system runs on the highest priority backend which is defined as:
```bash
./llama-tornado --gpu --model /opt/models/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf
Detected TornadoVM backends: cuda, opencl (from /home/thanos/repositories/TornadoVM/dist/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-cuda-opencl-linux-amd64/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-cuda-opencl/etc/tornado.backend) - using cuda (auto-selected)
```

#### To explicitly use the CUDA backend
```bash
./llama-tornado --gpu --model /opt/models/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf
Detected TornadoVM backends: cuda, opencl (from /home/thanos/repositories/TornadoVM/dist/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-cuda-opencl-linux-amd64/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-cuda-opencl/etc/tornado.backend) - using cuda
```

#### To explicitly use the OpenCL backend
```bash
./llama-tornado --gpu --opencl --model /opt/models/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf
Detected TornadoVM backends: cuda, opencl (from /home/thanos/repositories/TornadoVM/dist/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-cuda-opencl-linux-amd64/tornadovm-5.1.1-jdk25-dev-cuda-opencl/etc/tornado.backend) - using opencl (requested via --opencl)
```

However, there is the option to use the flag `--opencl`, `--metal`, `--cuda`,`--ptx` to explicitly ask to run with this backend.

items.title: Author Keycloak and Kafka context-benchmark suites
items.body:
Brings the benchmark corpus in line with the gallery, which now has 6 showcases (was 4 when the corpus was last authored). Adds two frozen suites and fixes a now-stale README line.

## New suites
- `docs/research/context-benchmark/tasks/keycloak.yaml` — 8 tasks
- `docs/research/context-benchmark/tasks/kafka.yaml` — 8 tasks

Both `yarramate/benchmark-suite/v1`, pinned to the exact commits the gallery models were built against (`73f08b39…` / `26b251a4…`). 4 comprehension (2 foundational + 2 multi-hop) + 2 change + 2 model-maintenance each.

## Multi-hop from the start
Per issue #56 (comprehension saturated at both model tiers in the 2026-07-29 sweep because the original tasks were single-hop), these two suites are built with multi-hop tasks from day one rather than needing a later v2 errata round:
- **Keycloak**: the federated-LDAP credential-check chain (login form → credential-manager dispatch → LDAP storage provider's `CredentialInputValidator` → the actual bind), and the identity-provider-deletion cascade (admin endpoint → `UserProvider#preRemove` → the JPA bulk-delete of federated-identity links, and what does/doesn't happen to the affected local accounts).
- **Kafka**: the `acks=all` acknowledgement path (`DelayedProduce` purgatory operation → `Partition.checkEnoughReplicasReachOffset` → the high-watermark/ISR condition, including the distinct "durably written but not-enough-replicas" error), and classic-protocol consumer-group rebalance (per-consumer offset auto-commit before revoke → broker-elected leader → leader-side `ConsumerPartitionAssignor` invocation).

Model-maintenance tasks extend the workspace into gaps the gallery's own discovery journeys already documented as intentionally out of scope (Keycloak: LDAP sync/import and the authorization-decision path as dynamic views; Kafka: producer idempotence and the transaction coordinator).

## Verification
- `node runner/validate-suite.mjs` passes for both new suites individually and in the full 11-file regression (all existing v1/v2 suites unaffected).
- **Ground truth was independently re-verified** against the pinned clones after drafting (not just trusted from the drafting pass) — this caught and fixed 3 real defects: two off-by-N line-number citations in the Kafka multi-hop tasks (verified via fresh reads against `/tmp/kafka-4.3.1`), and one comprehension prompt that incorrectly implied a method was private when it isn't (`maybeShrinkIsr` is package-visible, not private — the prompt and ground truth now state this explicitly rather than asserting a false premise).
- Every `verifiedAgainst`/`touches` citation passed an automated file-exists + line-in-bounds check, plus manual re-verification of every inline line-number claim in all four comprehension tasks per suite.

## README
Removed the stale "gallery currently provides 4 — add a fifth showcase" corpus warning; it now correctly states all 6 gallery showcases have benchmark suites, clearing the N≥5 headline-pooling threshold from DESIGN.md.

## Process note
The two subagents I originally dispatched to author these in parallel both failed immediately on an account-level `429 Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted` (not transient —~73h retry-after), so this was authored solo in the primary session using the exact investigation-and-citation contract I'd written for them, then independently re-verified as above.

items.title: Visualization page: performance patches, richer controls, and smoother interaction
items.body:
## Overview

This branch overhauls the study visualization page inner works. Main changes: 
- making slider and drag interactions achieve better perofrmance on large CBCT scans,
- expanding the control panel with  3D render tools
-  tightening lifecycle/cleanup around the Niivue viewer.

---

## Niivue performance patches (`patch-package`)

Adds `patch-package` (runs on `postinstall`) and five targeted fixes to `@niivue/niivue@0.68.1`. Full rationale and benchmarks live in `packages/application/frontend/patches/README.md`.

In plain terms, stock Niivue was doing a lot of redundant GPU work on every contrast/opacity/colormap tweak and on every mouse drag. These patches fix that:

1. **Skip unused gradient textures** - gradient lighting is never enabled in this app, but Niivue was still spending ~390 ms recomputing gradient textures on every refresh.
2. **Cache the raw 3D volume texture** - cal_min/cal_max/opacity/colormap changes no longer re-upload the entire voxel array (~500 ms saved per tweak on large float64 volumes).
3. **Pool output textures**- stops allocating and leaking ~180 MB GPU textures on every refresh; without this, sustained slider dragging eventually tanked frame rate to ~7 fps.
4. **Single draw per 3D rotation drag** - dragging to rotate the render tile used to trigger three full raycast frames per mousemove; now one.
5. **Remove redundant pre-draw on drags** - 2D slice drags (crosshair, windowing) drop from two `drawScene` calls per mousemove to one.

**Net effect:** `nv.updateGLVolume()` goes from ~920 ms → ~5 ms on typical scans, and continuous cal-slider dragging stays around ~25 ms/frame instead of degrading over time.

---

## New hook: `useNiivueSyncedRotation`

Extracts two-way binding between React state and Niivue’s 3D render rotation.

- Canvas drag updates flow back into the azimuth/elevation sliders via `onAzimuthElevationChange`.
- Slider changes push into Niivue via `setRenderAzimuthElevation`.
- Includes angle normalization and a `resetRotation()` helper.

This replaces manually duplicated rotation state that could drift out of sync with the canvas.

---

## VisualizationPage control panel & interaction

### New / improved controls
- **Multiplanar (4 Views)** layout option — grid layout with axial, coronal, sagittal, and 3D render tiles.
- **Global calibration ranges** — cal_min/cal_max sliders now use each volume’s `global_min`/`global_max` as bounds instead of hardcoded 0–100.
- **3D render zoom** — slider plus ± buttons; synced with Niivue via `onZoom3DChange`.
- **Clip plane** — depth range corrected to Niivue’s signed-distance model (−√3 … +√3), starting fully visible; azimuth and elevation sliders retained.
- **Reset Display Settings** — restores per-volume cal_min/cal_max (captured at load time), opacity, colormap, visibility, rotation, and zoom.

### Mouse wheel on the canvas
Replaces Niivue’s default wheel behavior with app-specific shortcuts:
- **Scroll** — zoom the 3D render in/out.
- **Shift + scroll** — nudge clip-plane depth.

### Smoother updates while dragging sliders
Niivue GPU updates are **batched per animation frame** via a keyed update queue (`queueNvUpdate`). Rapid slider events coalesce to one GPU pass per setting per frame, always applying the latest value. Different settings changed in the same frame (e.g. reset) still all apply.

### Guards & defaults
- cal_min cannot exceed cal_max (and vice versa); NaN/undefined inputs fall back to safe defaults.
- Named constants and enums for slice types, colormaps, ranges, and Niivue defaults — less magic numbers scattered through the component.
- Default volume/overlay display names simplified (`volume`, `overlay`).

### Loading & lifecycle
- Sidebar controls are **disabled and dimmed** while volumes are loading (`viewPhase !== "ready"`).
- Loading overlay with spinner and status text over the canvas.
- Proper teardown: `removeVolume` + `nv.cleanup()`, plus `URL.revokeObjectURL` for blob URLs created in volatile (in-memory) mode.

items.title: 09 containerization
items.body:
Packages the coordinator and each shard into Docker containers so that local dev and Chameleon Cloud deployments run identically.

**Changes**:

- **Two Dockerfiles**: `docker/coordinator/Dockerfile` (**heavy**: torch + sentence-transformers, model baked in at build time so startup is instant) and `docker/shard/Dockerfile` (*lean*: grpcio + sqlite-vec only). CPU-only torch wheels keep the coordinator image at ~1.7 GB rather than ~8 GB (great since we're not using a large embedder, and haven't relied on GPU availability at all).
- **`docker-compose.yml` for local dev**: coordinator + 3 shards on a bridge network, named volumes for shard persistence. Run with `docker compose up --build`.
- **Chameleon deployment scripts** in `deploy/chameleon/`: `start-coordinator.sh`, `start-shard.sh`, `start-benchmark.sh`, and a README with step-by-step instructions.
- **GitHub Actions workflow** (`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`) that builds and pushes both images to GHCR on every push to `main`. After merging, Mario needs to make both packages public on GHCR once (Profile → Packages → change visibility) so Chameleon nodes can pull without authenticating.
- **Proto stubs** (`src/vector_store_pb2.py`, `src/vector_store_pb2_grpc.py`) **are now committed** rather than gitignored, so images don't need `grpc_tools` at build time. **A pre-commit hook** (`scripts/pre-commit`) blocks commits where the stubs are out of sync with the proto. **Install with** `ln -s ../../scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit`. **Regenerate stubs with** `bash scripts/generate_protos.sh`.

items.title: Community benchmarks: PR-submitted numbers, zero telemetry

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

items.body:
## Summary

Stacks on top of #41. Lets users contribute their own NeuralMind reduction-ratio numbers **without** breaking the "nothing leaves your machine" brand promise — submissions happen through a PR (or an issue a maintainer converts to a PR), so every row is auditable, signed, and verifiable. Zero backend, zero telemetry.

**⚠ Base branch is `claude/self-benchmarking`, not `main`.** Once #41 merges, rebase/retarget this PR to `main` — or merge both together.

## What users see

1. **"Community benchmarks" section** in the README with an auto-rendered table of submissions and a clear "Submit yours" CTA.
2. **One-click issue form** at `/issues/new?template=community-benchmark.yml` — drop-downs for language + model, required fields for ratio / command / submitter, two consent checkboxes. No JSON authoring required for drive-by contributors.
3. **Direct PR path** for contributors who prefer JSON — add an entry to `docs/community-benchmarks.json` + run the render script.

## Data shape

`docs/community-benchmarks.json` seeded with the two reference entries (cmmc20, mempalace) already in the existing README. Schema (`docs/community-benchmarks.schema.json`) constrains:

- Required: `project_name`, `language`, `nodes`, `avg_reduction_ratio`, `date_submitted`, `submitted_by`, `verification_command`
- Optional: `repo_url`, `avg_wakeup_tokens`, `avg_query_tokens`, `queries_per_day`, `model`, `notes`
- Enums on `language` and `model` so entries aggregate cleanly
- Pattern constraints on `submitted_by` (GitHub username rules) and `date_submitted` (ISO 8601)

## Sanity beyond schema

`scripts/validate_community_benchmarks.py` adds four rules JSON Schema can't express:

- **No future dates** (catches copy-paste mistakes)
- **Plausible reduction ratios** (fails loudly if someone enters `97` when they meant `0.97` → `33×`)
- **No duplicate `(project, submitter)`** combos — updates are in-place edits, not duplicates
- **ISO-8601 date format** enforced with a real `date.fromisoformat`

## CI — `.github/workflows/validate-community-benchmarks.yml`

- Runs only on PRs that touch the JSON, schema, or scripts (no waste on unrelated PRs)
- Validates schema + sanity rules (fails build if anything's off)
- Re-renders the README table and fails the build if it's out of sync with the JSON — contributors must run `python scripts/render_community_table.py --inject README.md` before their PR merges

## Why not Option A (telemetry)?

The other path for "users upload their data" is opt-in telemetry — `neuralmind benchmark . --share` POSTing numbers to a hosted endpoint. Rejected because it would undermine the core privacy selling point that the landing page and comparison pages keep repeating. PR submissions give you the same data with zero infrastructure and higher trust (every row has a GitHub handle attached).

## Test plan

- [ ] Merging #41 first, then this PR cleanly rebases on main (or merge both together)
- [ ] Open an issue via the template → all required fields work → maintainer can convert the body into a JSON entry
- [ ] Add a test entry to `docs/community-benchmarks.json` → validation workflow runs → passes with valid entry, fails with bad date/ratio/duplicate
- [ ] `python scripts/render_community_table.py` prints the current table
- [ ] `python scripts/render_community_table.py --inject README.md` writes between the markers and leaves everything else alone
