Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

items.title: feat: v0.1 vertical slice - init, retrieval, Ukrainian locale, one adapter
items.body:
## Summary

Phase B2: the v0.1 vertical slice - the smallest complete, reproducible EIF
workflow. One synthetic demo project instance (`examples/demo-workspace/`),
initialized as a real, separately-runnable instance; seeded with real
knowledge; searched for real; changed with a real fix informed by that
retrieval; verified with a real failing-before/passing-after test; closed
out truthfully in Ukrainian; and the instance itself audited for integrity
from its own bundle.

This PR has been through three independent hardening reviews since it was
opened (2026-07-15). Each found real gaps between what the slice claimed
and what it actually did, and each was fixed in place rather than papered
over - see the commit history for the full per-round detail (`efc6736`
"heal the vertical slice", `f0cc722` "round 2 hardening", `d875293`/`fa29175`
"round 3 hardening"). This description reflects the **current, final**
state only - stale round-1/round-2 commands, counts, and open items have
been removed rather than layered.

## Architecture (current)

- **Config/lock split.** `.eif/config.yaml` is user-owned (project name,
  adapter, locale, governance) and is never touched by a routine upgrade.
  `.eif/framework.lock.yaml` is EIF-managed provenance (exact framework
  commit, dirty flag, `ref_verification: git-verified|asserted`, a
  sha256-hashed bundle manifest with a combined digest, the generated
  adapter entrypoint), fully regenerated every init/upgrade. See
  [`docs/architecture/instance-contract.md`](docs/architecture/instance-contract.md).
- **Three explicit modes, decided by what's on disk, not by which flags
  happen to be passed.** `init` (no config yet, `--project-name`
  required); `upgrade` (config exists, no `--force` - project/adapter/
  locale/migration-status all come from the existing config and lock;
  any of those flags passed anyway are ignored with a printed note, never
  silently applied); `reconfigure` (`--force` - an explicit flag wins,
  anything unpassed keeps its current value, existing config backed up
  first).
- **One transaction for the full managed state.** Config (when written),
  runtime bundle, lock, entrypoint, and `.gitignore` each stage to a
  `.next` path and commit as one ordered sequence of atomic renames. If
  any stage fails, every already-committed stage in that run rolls back
  to its exact prior content, and any staged-but-never-reached `.next`
  file is cleaned up - not just the runtime swap, and not just a
  preflight check.
- **Marker-safe entrypoint/`.gitignore` merges.** `CLAUDE.md` and
  `.gitignore` updates go through `eif_markers.py`, which refuses to
  write anything if the existing `BEGIN`/`END` markers are missing a
  partner, reversed, or duplicated, instead of silently corrupting
  content around them.
- **Self-verification.** `scripts/eif_verify_runtime.py`, bundled into
  every instance, checks config/lock schema validity, manifest digest
  self-consistency, every manifested file's hash, missing/unexpected
  files (`README.md`/`__pycache__` excluded by design), config/adapter-
  registry/lock/entrypoint consistency, provenance notes, and marker
  integrity, in one pass, from the instance's own bundle.
- **Truthful rendering.** `scripts/eif_render.py` reads
  `documentation_locale` from `.eif/config.yaml` by default and writes
  real files. A config that exists but is broken fails loudly instead of
  silently rendering in English (a missing config is a different,
  legitimate case). A "final" render with any unresolved `{placeholder}`
  fails by default; `--draft` explicitly opts into a partial render.
  Writes are atomic.
- **Lifecycle- and schema-aware retrieval.** `eif_search_knowledge.py`
  returns only eligible statuses by default and reports unparseable-YAML,
  schema-invalid, and status-ineligible as three distinct outcomes, never
  confused with "no results." The generated `CLAUDE.md` search command
  includes `--framework-root` by default.
- **Restricted adapter registry.** `--adapter` only accepts a registered
  name (`scripts/eif_adapters.py`); `eif_init` generates `CLAUDE.md` (the
  file Claude Code actually loads, per official docs) via that registry,
  not a hardcoded guess.

## Commands (current, all re-run this session)

```
# init
python scripts/eif_init.py --framework-root . --instance-path <path> --project-name <name> --locale uk
# routine upgrade - no flags needed, driven by the existing config/lock
python scripts/eif_init.py --framework-root . --instance-path <path>
# explicit reconfiguration - only the flags passed change anything
python scripts/eif_init.py --framework-root . --instance-path <path> --force --locale en

python .eif/runtime/eif_search_knowledge.py --knowledge-root knowledge --framework-root .eif/runtime "<query>"
python .eif/runtime/eif_verify_runtime.py --framework-root .eif/runtime
python .eif/runtime/eif_render.py --framework-root .eif/runtime knowledge-delta
python .eif/runtime/eif_render.py --framework-root .eif/runtime session-closeout --set task_name="..." --set branch_or_pr="..." --set verification_result="..." --set artifacts="..." --set promoted="..." --set not_done="..." --set open_questions="..."

python scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --framework-root . --instance-root <path> "knowledge/**/*.md"
python scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --framework-root . --config <path>/.eif/config.yaml
python scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --framework-root . --lock <path>/.eif/framework.lock.yaml
python scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py --repo .
python scripts/eif_check_links.py --repo .
```

## Tests

11 suites, 234 checks, all passing locally and reproduced identically from
a fresh `git clone` to a temporary directory outside the repository:

`test_validate.py` 15, `test_privacy_scan.py` 19, `test_knowledge_delta.py`
6, `test_generate_index.py` 12, `test_search_knowledge.py` 11,
`test_locale.py` 7, `test_render.py` 22, `test_markers.py` 12,
`test_verify_runtime.py` 17, `test_init.py` 38, `test_journey.py` 75.

`test_journey.py` is a real subprocess journey (not internal-function
calls) covering: init/upgrade/reconfigure against a real seed project;
config/lock schema validation; runtime materialization; English +
Ukrainian retrieval; task-scope; a failing-before/passing-after behavioral
test; config-driven Ukrainian Knowledge Delta + closeout written to real
files; artifact/privacy/link validation from the instance's own bundle;
a routine upgrade proven to preserve a `migration_status: adopted` set by
an earlier explicit reconfigure, with zero flags on the upgrade itself;
the generated search command's `--framework-root`; strict-vs-`--draft`
rendering; `eif_verify_runtime.py` against a clean instance and against
each of: a hand-edited bundle file, a schema-invalid lock, and reversed
entrypoint markers; a second, fully independent instance; and, for each
of the four post-config transaction stages (runtime, lock, entrypoint,
`.gitignore`) in turn, a real injected failure immediately after that
stage commits, followed by confirming every already-committed stage
restored to its exact prior byte-for-byte content, zero orphaned
`.next`/`.previous` files, and the instance passing both
`eif_verify_runtime.py` and a real retrieval command afterward.

Also re-run from the clean clone: the demo's own behavioral test
(`examples/demo-workspace/tests/test_calendar_utils.py`), a privacy scan
and link check (0 findings, both empty), and a YAML/JSON-Schema
self-consistency check over every schema file.

CI on the current head (`fa29175`): **6/6 jobs green** - Privacy scan,
Frontmatter and config schema validation, Vertical slice, Relative link
check, YAML and JSON Schema syntax check, Knowledge Delta completeness.

## Adapter evidence

`adapters/claude-code/README.md`. Claude Code CLI `2.1.169`, verified live
2026-07-15. Official docs confirm Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.md` at session
start. Persistent-instruction and skill discovery OBSERVED directly in the
sessions that built this slice. Hook rewrite behavior is **not**
re-verified end-to-end this round - carried over from the private
instance's dated (2026-06-16) evidence, with a note on what
re-verification would require. No hook scripts shipped (out of scope).
Every command above runs with zero dependency on any hook.

## Ukrainian locale evidence

Three real output surfaces: status messages (`eif_init.py`, e.g.
`Ініціалізація EIF project instance у ...`), Knowledge Delta
(`examples/demo-workspace/knowledge-delta.md`), and closeout
(`examples/demo-workspace/session-closeout.md`), all rendered by the
config-driven command above with no `--locale` flag. English fallback
verified for both "no config" and "unknown locale" - distinct from a
broken config, which now fails loudly instead of silently defaulting to
English. Framework identifiers, schemas, commands, and code stay English
throughout. **D-06/D-07 remain open** - this slice is evidence for that
future decision, not a substitute for it.

## Privacy statement

`python scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py --repo .` against the final tree, and
independently against the clean clone: 0 absolute-path leaks, 0
secret-shaped findings, 0 denylisted-token findings, both times. No
private repository names, machine paths, or owner-identifying detail were
introduced.

## Knowledge Delta

### New facts
- A routine upgrade that silently applies CLI defaults instead of the
  existing config is a real, severe bug class, not a hypothetical -
  reproduced live this round: a bare re-run without repeating
  `--locale`/`--migration-status` reset both to CLI defaults and
  overwrote `migration_status: adopted` with `greenfield` in the
  committed lock file.
- `os.replace()`/file rename is atomic on both POSIX and Windows, but a
  sequence of several such renames is not - the previous "transactional
  runtime swap" left the lock/entrypoint/`.gitignore` writes unprotected;
  a `_Stage`/`commit_transaction` primitive generalizes the same
  stage/commit/rollback shape to any file or directory.
- A schema's top-level `required` array and a nested object's own
  `required` array are independent - `framework-lock.schema.json` had
  `instance.migration_status` conditionally required only if `instance`
  itself was present, but `instance` was never in the top-level
  `required` list, so a lock missing the entire `instance` block passed
  schema validation. Found by a test written to be that specific negative
  case, not by manual review.

### New rules
- Do not let a schema-driven required field spread silently: when a
  schema gains a new required top-level object (here: `adapter` on
  `eif-config.schema.json`), every existing fixture/example/generated
  instance that predates it must be re-validated, not assumed still
  valid - a stale hand-written fixture (`scripts/tests/fixtures/config/
  positive.yaml`) and a stale generated instance
  (`examples/demo-workspace/.eif/framework.lock.yaml`, missing the new
  `ref_verification` field) both would have started failing silently
  otherwise; both caught before push by re-running the exact CI commands
  locally against a clean clone, not assumed from the suite's own
  internal test count.
- A test-only fault-injection env var, checked immediately after a stage
  commits (not before, not mid-rename), is a more honest and more
  reproducible way to prove rollback than a synthetic preflight failure -
  it exercises the real rollback code path at a real, named boundary
  instead of a code path that never reaches the transaction at all.

### Rejected hypotheses
- Considered enforcing `adapter.name` as a JSON Schema `enum` alongside
  the Python registry - rejected: two independently-maintained lists of
  the same valid values silently drift; kept the registry as the sole
  source of truth, cross-checked at runtime by `eif_verify_runtime.py`
  instead.
- Considered treating the marker-conflict refusal in `eif_init.py` as
  equivalent evidence to the transaction-rollback tests - rejected: one
  is a preflight refusal (nothing staged or written), the other is a
  mid-transaction rollback of already-committed stages; conflating them
  in the claims ledger would overstate what either test actually proves.

### Incidents
- None this round beyond the two staleness bugs already described under
  New rules (both fixed before push, neither reached CI red on the
  pushed commit).

### Promote to shared knowledge base?
[x] yes - the "routine upgrade must be driven by existing config, not CLI
defaults" lesson and the "a schema's nested `required` doesn't imply the
parent key is required" lesson are both general, not specific to this
framework. Not auto-promoted to `core/` - flagged for owner ratification,
consistent with the authority model's framework-vs-project scope
distinction.

### Updated knowledge files
- `docs/product/claims-evidence.md` (evidence, counts, and two new claim
  rows updated/added - see the diff)
- `README.md` (bootstrap-script and new self-verification capability rows
  updated)

## Claims evidence

`docs/product/claims-evidence.md` is the source of truth for what public
copy is allowed to say - updated this round with current test counts and
two new OBSERVED rows (config-driven upgrade + full transaction; instance
self-verification). Still **UNVERIFIED**: token savings, task-quality/
rework improvement. Still **NOT TESTED**: Graphify, RTK.

## Remaining open decisions

Unchanged by this PR - see `core/policies/decisions.md`: D-02, D-03, D-05
(CLI name - `eif_init.py` remains explicitly labeled experimental), D-06/
D-07 (language), D-08 (dependency model), D-09 (required adapters), D-10
through D-12 remain provisional/open.

## Deferred capabilities

Full execution-packet machinery, curator/active-learning, cross-repo
knowledge sync, a second adapter, Graphify, RTK - all explicitly out of
scope for this slice, not silently dropped. See the private migration
ledger (a private companion planning repository, PR #59, merged
2026-07-15 - not linked here since it contains private paths).

## Recommended next steps

Not started here, per this PR's own scope:
1. A real-project pilot (see the separate pilot-readiness proposal posted
   in this session's report - explicitly not the private companion planning repository).
2. Merge-gate hardening: explicit required-check names, `SKIPPED`/
   `NEUTRAL` treatment, unresolved-review-thread handling, override audit
   trail.
3. A second adapter, once the framework/adapter boundary has been proven
   to hold on a real pilot, not just in this synthetic demo.

Graphify/RTK integration, a quality-per-token benchmark, and public-ready
README/demo-recording/website work remain sequenced after those.

## Not merging

This agent will not merge this PR, per this task's explicit instruction.

Updates `hono` from 4.11.6 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

items.title: feat(codegraph): integrate CodeGraph MCP server to cut review token usage
items.body:
## What

- Opportunistically integrate [CodeGraph](https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) (a local MCP server that pre-indexes a codebase into a SQLite knowledge graph) into the PR-review launch flow, across four independent tiers:
  - **Tier 1 — prompt nudge.** New `CODEGRAPH_HINT_SUFFIX` appended to the review prompt when `.codegraph/` is present in the workspace, steering agents to the six core MCP tools (`codegraph_context`, `codegraph_impact`, `codegraph_callers`, `codegraph_callees`, `codegraph_trace`, `codegraph_search`) instead of grep+Read fan-out.
  - **Tier 2 — auto-sync.** Runs `codegraph sync` after `gh pr checkout` so the index reflects the checked-out branch before the agent starts querying (CodeGraph's file-watcher only runs while the CLI is alive).
  - **Tier 3 — opt-in init helper.** New persisted `x` keybinding/toggle (`codegraph_assist` in `settings`). When on AND `.codegraph/` is missing AND `codegraph` is on PATH, prompts the user once per launch to run `codegraph init --index`. Default off — missing-index workspaces stay silent.
  - **Tier 4 — affected-tests injection.** Chains `gh pr view --json baseRefName` → `git diff origin/<base>...HEAD --name-only` → `codegraph affected --stdin --quiet`, then inlines the resulting test paths as a scoping hint for the pr-test-analyzer agent. Capped at 50 with overflow note.

## Why

- CodeGraph's published benchmark is ~35% cheaper / ~57% fewer tokens / ~71% fewer tool calls for a single agent answering a single architecture question. cc-reviewer is the **multiplicative** case — every launch fans out into 6 sub-agents (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, type-design-analyzer, comment-analyzer, pr-test-analyzer, code-simplifier), each independently grepping and reading. Expected savings meet or exceed the published numbers.
- The workspace at `$GH_PR_WORKSPACE/<owner>/<repo>` is **reused across every PR review of that repo** (clone-once, fetch-after) — that's exactly CodeGraph's amortisation model. Index once, query many times across many PR reviews.
- Tier 4 is the most cc-reviewer-specific value-add: `codegraph affected` doesn't show up in CodeGraph's own docs as a review-workflow tool, but it directly improves the pr-test-analyzer agent's ability to scope coverage gaps to the diff.

## How

- New constants & helpers in `cc_pr_reviewer/__init__.py`:
  - `CODEGRAPH_HINT_SUFFIX` (Tier 1 prompt block)
  - `CODEGRAPH_AFFECTED_TESTS_CAP = 50` (Tier 4 list size cap)
  - `format_codegraph_affected_tests(paths)` — pure renderer: dedup + sort + cap + overflow note + framing prose. Returns `""` as a skip-section sentinel.
  - `_collect_codegraph_affected(local_path, number)` — chains the gh→git→codegraph shell-out, returns `[]` on any failure with a printed warning (non-fatal degradation).
- `build_review_prompt` gains two new kwargs (`codegraph_present: bool = False`, `codegraph_affected_tests: str = ""`), both with back-compat defaults. The new sections land between reviewer extras and the existing-comments block so both CodeGraph sections are contiguous.
- `_launch_claude` orchestration after `gh pr checkout`:
  1. Probe `.codegraph/`. If missing and the `x` toggle is on, prompt the user to init.
  2. If present, run `codegraph sync` (incremental, idempotent).
  3. If present, run `_collect_codegraph_affected` and render the block.
  4. Thread both into `build_review_prompt`.
- New `x` binding + `action_toggle_codegraph` mirror the existing `c` toggle pattern (cycle, persist to `settings`, refresh footer indicator, notify).
- All four hooks are silent no-ops when `codegraph` isn't on PATH or `.codegraph/` is absent — zero behaviour change for users who haven't installed CodeGraph.

## Can this PR break any existing features. If yes, please list possible items. If no, please explain why. (PS: Admins do not merge the PR without this section filled)

- No behaviour change for users without CodeGraph installed: every new hook gates on `(local_path / ".codegraph").is_dir()` and/or `shutil.which("codegraph") is not None`. When the user hasn't run `codegraph install`, no new prints, no new prompt sections, no new shell-outs.
- `build_review_prompt`'s two new kwargs both default to `False`/`""`, so the existing test fixtures and any external callers keep producing the same prompts byte-for-byte. The full canonical-order test was preserved unchanged; new tests cover the CodeGraph-on paths separately.
- `subprocess.call` exit codes from `codegraph sync` / `codegraph init` / `codegraph affected` are surfaced as warnings, not errors — the agent still launches, the prompt just lacks a section. Tier 4's collector returns `[]` on any subprocess failure with a printed warning.
- The new `x` keybinding is unbound on the existing footer; no collision with current bindings (`r/f5, enter, o, d, m, f, g, s, c, u, q`).

## Database Migrations

- None for the SQLite migration system. The new `codegraph_assist` setting uses the existing `settings` K/V table (`_get_setting` / `_set_setting`); writing a new key on first toggle is automatic and reads default to `"0"` when absent.

## Env Config

- No new env vars. CodeGraph itself is configured globally via `codegraph install` (writes per-CLI MCP config to `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, etc.) — cc-reviewer just opportunistically uses the binary when it's on PATH.

## Relevant Docs

- CodeGraph project: https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph
- CodeGraph benchmark methodology and per-repo numbers: README "Why CodeGraph?" section in the upstream repo.
- No CLAUDE.md updates in this PR — the integration is invisible to users who haven't installed CodeGraph. A follow-up could document the `x` toggle and the recommended `codegraph install --target=claude,codex --location=global --yes` prereq.

## Related Issues or PRs

-

## Dependencies Versions

- No new Python dependencies. CodeGraph is an optional external CLI (Node-based, installed via `npx @colbymchenry/codegraph` or the install.sh script); cc-reviewer treats it as a runtime-detected tool just like `gh`, `git`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`.

## Notes on Testing

- 10 new unit tests in `tests/test_cc_pr_reviewer.py` covering the pure helpers and prompt-assembly seams:
  - `CODEGRAPH_HINT_SUFFIX` absent by default / present when flagged (parameterised across all three CLIs)
  - Canonical section order with the hint in place
  - The hint mentions every one of the six core MCP tools (guards against decay to generic prose)
  - `format_codegraph_affected_tests`: empty list → empty sentinel, whitespace-only paths drop, dedup + sort, cap + overflow note, exactly-at-cap doesn't lie with "truncated"
  - Full assembly with both CodeGraph sections present (parameterised across all three CLIs) — locks contiguous ordering
  - The two CodeGraph kwargs are independently gated (a future caller can ship the block without claiming index presence)
- Full suite: 104 tests pass. `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format .` both clean. Pre-commit hook passed on commit.
- Integration testing (live `codegraph` binary + real PR launch) is out of scope for the unit suite — same pattern as the existing `gh`/`claude`/`codex`/`gemini` subprocess flows. Would need an explicit manual run against a repo that has `.codegraph/` initialised.

## Screenshots

## Checklist

I have read and understood the [Contribution Guidelines].

Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Release notes

Sourced from path-to-regexp's releases.

v8.4.2

Fixed

  • Error on trailing backslash (#434) 9a78879

Performance

  • Minimize array allocations (#437) 937c02d
  • Improve compile performance (#436) 57247e6
    • Should improve compilation performance by ~25%
  • Remove internal tokenization during parse (#435) 5844988
    • Should improve parse performance by ~20%

Bundle size to 1.93 kB, from 1.97 kB.

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.1...v8.4.2

v8.4.1

Fixed

  • Remove trie deduplication (#431) 6bc8e84
    • Using a trie required non-greedy matching, which regressed wildcards in non-ending mode by matching them up until the first match. For example:
      • /*foo with /a/b = /a
      • /*foo.htmlwith /a/b.html/c.html = /a/b.html
  • Allow backtrack handling to match itself (#427) 5bcd30b
    • When backtracking was introduced, it rejected matching things like /:"a"_:"b" against /foo__. This makes intuitive sense because the second parameter is not going to backtrack on _ anymore, but it's somewhat unexpected since there's no reason it shouldn't match the second _.

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.0...v8.4.1

v8.4.0

Important

  • Fix CVE-2026-4926 (GHSA-j3q9-mxjg-w52f)
  • Fix CVE-2026-4923 (GHSA-27v5-c462-wpq7)

Fixed

  • Restricts wildcard backtracking when using more than 1 in a path (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#421)

Changed

  • Dedupes regex prefixes (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#422)
    • This will result in shorter regular expressions for some cases using optional groups
  • Rejects large optional route combinations (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#424)
    • When using groups such as /users{/delete} it will restrict the number of generated combinations to < 256, equivalent to 8 top-level optional groups and unlikely to occur in a real world application, but avoids exploding the regex size for applications that accept user created routes

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Release notes

v8.4.2

Fixed

Performance

  • Minimize array allocations (#437) 937c02d

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.1...v8.4.2

v8.4.1

Fixed

  • Remove trie deduplication (#431) 6bc8e84
    • Using a trie required non-greedy matching, which regressed wildcards in non-ending mode by matching them up until the first match. For example:
      • /*foo with /a/b = /a
      • /*foo.htmlwith /a/b.html/c.html = /a/b.html
  • Allow backtrack handling to match itself (#427) 5bcd30b
    • When backtracking was introduced, it rejected matching things like /:"a"_:"b" against /foo__. This makes intuitive sense because the second parameter is not going to backtrack on _ anymore, but it's somewhat unexpected since there's no reason it shouldn't match the second _.

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.0...v8.4.1

v8.4.0

Important

  • Fix CVE-2026-4926 (GHSA-j3q9-mxjg-w52f)
  • Fix CVE-2026-4923 (GHSA-27v5-c462-wpq7)

Fixed

  • Restricts wildcard backtracking when using more than 1 in a path (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#421)

Changed

  • Dedupes regex prefixes (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#422)
    • This will result in shorter regular expressions for some cases using optional groups
  • Rejects large optional route combinations (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#424)
    • When using groups such as /users{/delete} it will restrict the number of generated combinations to < 256, equivalent to 8 top-level optional groups and unlikely to occur in a real world application, but avoids exploding the regex size for applications that accept user created routes

Bumps the npm_and_yarn group with 4 updates in the /api directory: [lodash](https://github.com/lodash/lodash), [ajv](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv), [brace-expansion](https://github.com/juliangruber/brace-expansion) and [path-to-regexp](https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp). Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash.omit
  • lodash.template

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

Updates `hono` from 4.12.5 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep

v8.4.1

    • Using a trie required non-greedy matching, which regressed wildcards in non-ending mode by matching them up until the first match. For example:

  • Allow backtrack handling to match itself (#427) 5bcd30b
    • When backtracking was introduced, it rejected matching things like /:"a"_:"b" against /foo__. This makes intuitive sense because the second parameter is not going to backtrack on _ anymore, but it's somewhat unexpected since there's no reason it shouldn't match the second _.

Updates `hono` from 4.12.9 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Updates `hono` from 4.11.4 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash.omit
  • lodash.template

Updates `path-to-regexp` from 8.3.0 to 8.4.2
Release notes

Sourced from path-to-regexp's releases.

v8.4.2

Fixed

  • Error on trailing backslash (#434) 9a78879

Performance

  • Minimize array allocations (#437) 937c02d
  • Improve compile performance (#436) 57247e6
    • Should improve compilation performance by ~25%
  • Remove internal tokenization during parse (#435) 5844988
    • Should improve parse performance by ~20%

Bundle size to 1.93 kB, from 1.97 kB.

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.1...v8.4.2

v8.4.1

Fixed

  • Remove trie deduplication (#431) 6bc8e84
    • Using a trie required non-greedy matching, which regressed wildcards in non-ending mode by matching them up until the first match. For example:
      • /*foo with /a/b = /a
      • /*foo.htmlwith /a/b.html/c.html = /a/b.html
  • Allow backtrack handling to match itself (#427) 5bcd30b
    • When backtracking was introduced, it rejected matching things like /:"a"_:"b" against /foo__. This makes intuitive sense because the second parameter is not going to backtrack on _ anymore, but it's somewhat unexpected since there's no reason it shouldn't match the second _.

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.0...v8.4.1

v8.4.0

Important

  • Fix CVE-2026-4926 (GHSA-j3q9-mxjg-w52f)
  • Fix CVE-2026-4923 (GHSA-27v5-c462-wpq7)

Fixed

  • Restricts wildcard backtracking when using more than 1 in a path (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#421)

Changed

  • Dedupes regex prefixes (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#422)
    • This will result in shorter regular expressions for some cases using optional groups
  • Rejects large optional route combinations (pillarjs/path-to-regexp#424)
    • When using groups such as /users{/delete} it will restrict the number of generated combinations to < 256, equivalent to 8 top-level optional groups and unlikely to occur in a real world application, but avoids exploding the regex size for applications that accept user created routes

Updates `axios` from 1.13.5 to 1.15.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.15.0

This release delivers two critical security patches, adds runtime support for Deno and Bun, and includes significant CI hardening, documentation improvements, and routine dependency updates.

⚠️ Important Changes

  • Deprecation: url.parse() usage has been replaced to address Node.js deprecation warnings. If you are on a recent version of Node.js, this resolves console warnings you may have been seeing. (#10625)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Proxy Handling: Fixed a no_proxy hostname normalisation bypass that could lead to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). (#10661)
  • Header Injection: Fixed an unrestricted cloud metadata exfiltration vulnerability via a header injection chain. (#10660)

🚀 New Features

  • Runtime Support: Added compatibility checks and documentation for Deno and Bun environments. (#10652, #10653)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • CI Security: Hardened workflow permissions to least privilege, added the zizmor security scanner, pinned action versions, and gated npm publishing with OIDC and environment protection. (#10618, #10619, #10627, #10637, #10666)
  • Dependencies: Bumped serialize-javascript, handlebars, picomatch, vite, and denoland/setup-deno to latest versions. Added a 7-day Dependabot cooldown period. (#10574, #10572, #10568, #10663, #10664, #10665, #10669, #10670, #10616)
  • Documentation: Unified docs, improved beforeRedirect credential leakage example, clarified withCredentials/withXSRFToken behaviour, HTTP/2 support notes, async/await timeout error handling, header case preservation, and various typo fixes. (#10649, #10624, #7452, #7471, #10654, #10644, #10589)
  • Housekeeping: Removed stale files, regenerated lockfile, and updated sponsor scripts and blocks. (#10584, #10650, #10582, #10640, #10659, #10668)
  • Tests: Added regression coverage for urlencoded Content-Type casing. (#10573)

🌟 New Contributors

We are thrilled to welcome our new contributors. Thank you for helping improve Axios:

  • @​Kilros0817 (#10625)
  • @​ashstrc (#10624)

v1.14.0

This release focuses on compatibility fixes, adapter stability improvements, and test/tooling modernisation.

⚠️ Important Changes

  • Breaking Changes: None identified in this release.
  • Action Required: If you rely on env-based proxy behaviour or CJS resolution edge-cases, validate your integration after upgrade (notably proxy-from-env v2 alignment and main entry compatibility fix).

🚀 New Features

  • Runtime Features: No new end-user features were introduced in this release.
  • Test Coverage Expansion: Added broader smoke/module test coverage for CJS and ESM package usage. (#7510)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Headers: Trim trailing CRLF in normalised header values. (#7456)
  • HTTP/2: Close detached HTTP/2 sessions on timeout to avoid lingering sessions. (#7457)
  • Fetch Adapter: Cancel ReadableStream created during request-stream capability probing to prevent async resource leaks. (#7515)
  • Proxy Handling: Fixed env proxy behavior with proxy-from-env v2 usage. (#7499)

Sourced from axios's changelog.

v1.15.0 — April 7, 2026

This release delivers two critical security patches targeting header injection and SSRF via proxy bypass, adds official runtime support for Deno and Bun, and includes significant CI security hardening.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Header Injection (CRLF): Rejects any header value containing \r or \n characters to block CRLF injection chains that could be used to exfiltrate cloud metadata (IMDS). Behavior change: headers with CR/LF now throw "Invalid character in header content". (#10660)

  • SSRF via no_proxy Bypass: Introduces a shouldBypassProxy helper that normalises hostnames (strips trailing dots, handles bracketed IPv6) before evaluating no_proxy/NO_PROXY rules, closing a gap that could cause loopback or internal hosts to be inadvertently proxied. (#10661)

🚀 New Features

  • Deno & Bun Runtime Support: Added full smoke test suites for Deno and Bun, with CI workflows that run both runtimes before any release is cut. (#10652)

Updates `hono` from 4.12.8 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend

Updates `hono` from 4.11.4 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.25.0

This release deliberately contains backwards-incompatible changes. To avoid automatically picking up releases like this, you should either be pinning the exact version of esbuild in your package.json file (recommended) or be using a version range syntax that only accepts patch upgrades such as ^0.24.0 or ~0.24.0. See npm's documentation about semver for more information.

  • Restrict access to esbuild's development server (GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99)

    This change addresses esbuild's first security vulnerability report. Previously esbuild set the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to * to allow esbuild's development server to be flexible in how it's used for development. However, this allows the websites you visit to make HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server, which gives read-only access to your source code if the website were to fetch your source code's specific URL. You can read more information in the report.

    Starting with this release, CORS will now be disabled, and requests will now be denied if the host does not match the one provided to --serve=. The default host is 0.0.0.0, which refers to all of the IP addresses that represent the local machine (e.g. both 127.0.0.1 and 192.168.0.1). If you want to customize anything about esbuild's development server, you can put a proxy in front of esbuild and modify the incoming and/or outgoing requests.

    In addition, the serve() API call has been changed to return an array of hosts instead of a single host string. This makes it possible to determine all of the hosts that esbuild's development server will accept.

    Thanks to @​sapphi-red for reporting this issue.

  • Delete output files when a build fails in watch mode (#3643)

    It has been requested for esbuild to delete files when a build fails in watch mode. Previously esbuild left the old files in place, which could cause people to not immediately realize that the most recent build failed. With this release, esbuild will now delete all output files if a rebuild fails. Fixing the build error and triggering another rebuild will restore all output files again.

  • Fix correctness issues with the CSS nesting transform (#3620, #3877, #3933, #3997, #4005, #4037, #4038)

    This release fixes the following problems:

    • Naive expansion of CSS nesting can result in an exponential blow-up of generated CSS if each nesting level has multiple selectors. Previously esbuild sometimes collapsed individual nesting levels using :is() to limit expansion. However, this collapsing wasn't correct in some cases, so it has been removed to fix correctness issues.

      /* Original code */
.parent {
  > .a,
  > .b1 > .b2 {
    color: red;
  }
}

      /* Old output (with --supported:nesting=false) */
      
.parent > :is(.a, .b1 > .b2) {
      
color: red;
      
}
      

      /* New output (with --supported:nesting=false) */
      
.parent > .a,
      
.parent > .b1 > .b2 {
      
color: red;
      
}

      Thanks to @​tim-we for working on a fix.

    • The & CSS nesting selector can be repeated multiple times to increase CSS specificity. Previously esbuild ignored this possibility and incorrectly considered && to have the same specificity as &. With this release, this should now work correctly:

      /* Original code (color should be red) */

Changelog: 2023

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2023 (versions 0.16.13 through 0.19.11).

0.19.11

  • Fix TypeScript-specific class transform edge case (#3559)

    The previous release introduced an optimization that avoided transforming super() in the class constructor for TypeScript code compiled with useDefineForClassFields set to false if all class instance fields have no initializers. The rationale was that in this case, all class instance fields are omitted in the output so no changes to the constructor are needed. However, if all of this is the case and there are #private instance fields with initializers, those private instance field initializers were still being moved into the constructor. This was problematic because they were being inserted before the call to super() (since super() is now no longer transformed in that case). This release introduces an additional optimization that avoids moving the private instance field initializers into the constructor in this edge case, which generates smaller code, matches the TypeScript compiler's output more closely, and avoids this bug:

    // Original code
class Foo extends Bar {
  #private = 1;
  public: any;
  constructor() {
    super();
  }
}

    // Old output (with esbuild v0.19.9)
    
class Foo extends Bar {
    
constructor() {
    
super();
    
this.#private = 1;
    
}
    
#private;
    
}
    

    // Old output (with esbuild v0.19.10)
    
class Foo extends Bar {
    
constructor() {
    
this.#private = 1;
    
super();
    
}
    
#private;
    
}
    

    // New output
    
class Foo extends Bar {
    
#private = 1;
    
constructor() {
    
super();
    
}
    
}

    The minifier previously allowed reordering a side-effect past a primitive, but didn't handle the case of reordering a primitive past a side-effect. This additional case is now handled:

Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `hono` from 4.12.0 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.
